the performance of the system is sensitive to the fraction of users that are equipped with in- vehicle navigation systems, that the performance of such systems is also sensitive to the behavioral assumptions that are used to represent the user responses to the supplied real time information, and that the framework provides a useful tool to investigate such effects and other questions of interest in this field.

(1) the effect of in vehicle information on system performance is highly dependent on the user behavioral response mechanism; (2) the system performance is sensitive to the fraction of users with in vehicle information; and (3) the system performance can be improved by providing information on the local conditions at the origin and the destination, as opposed to information on the overall system conditions.
the effect of in vehicle information systems on system performance depends on the fraction of users with such systems, the information provided, and the users' response to the provided information.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the effect of the in-vehicle information strategies on overall system performance is very much dependent on user responses, and that the effect of information strategies can be positive, neutral or negative, depending on user responses.
, while the use of information systems may improve the system performance in some cases, in other cases the use of information may have a detrimental effect on the system performance.

the performance of real-time in-vehicle information strategies is sensitive to the behavioral response of users, and that a more realistic representation of user behavior is likely to result in a more realistic assessment of the potential of real-time information strategies to improve the performance of a traffic corridor.
